claim: This manifest inventories Cohort's retention controls. It does not certify complete GDPR compliance or adjudicate whether a legal minimum, hold, or erasure request is legally justified. Evidence identities are structurally linked here; execution is established only by successful test runs.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: executable compliance inventory
requirements.requirement: Every supported manifest entry names structurally linked xUnit evidence, every dedicated corpus test is linked by the manifest, and statuses and evidence kinds use closed vocabularies; successful test execution is a separate gate.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: annotation-driven retention scope
requirements.requirement: Entities marked Retain participate, while unannotated and ExemptFromRetention entities remain outside mutation scope.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: fail-closed model validation
requirements.requirement: Conflicting Retain and ExemptFromRetention annotations fail validation before mutation.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: unsupported relational model shapes
requirements.requirement: Owned, shared-table, and table-split retained mappings fail hosted startup and direct public execution before seeded rows can be mutated.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: inheritance mappings are unsupported
requirements.requirement: A retained entity participating in an EF inheritance hierarchy fails hosted startup and direct public execution before seeded rows can be mutated.

requirements.source: UK GDPR Article 5(1)(e), storage limitation
requirements.requirement: Ordinary sweeps process rows strictly older than the resolved cutoff and preserve unexpired rows and rows exactly on the cutoff.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: explicit null-anchor accountability
requirements.requirement: Zero retention permits immediate scheduled eligibility, while null anchors survive scheduled sweeps and are reported.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: contextual policy resolution
requirements.requirement: Rule resolution receives the target tenant and logical time, and ordinary sweeps use the greater of Period and LegalMin.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: explicit exemption strategy
requirements.requirement: Strategy.Exempt produces a visible zero-mutation result while preserving matching rows.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: purge semantics
requirements.requirement: Purge physically removes only eligible rows.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: soft-delete semantics
requirements.requirement: Soft delete changes only configured deletion markers and does not repeat completed deletion.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: anonymisation semantics
requirements.requirement: Anonymise changes only declared fields, preserves non-personal fields, and does not repeatedly anonymise marked rows.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: provider-aware anonymisation values
requirements.requirement: Factory-backed anonymisation reads original values in their CLR representation and converts generated output to the configured provider representation.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: strategy-specific startup validation
requirements.requirement: Invalid soft-delete and anonymise model metadata fails validation before execution.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant informed by UK GDPR Article 17(3)
requirements.requirement: Ordinary sweeps apply max(Period, LegalMin), keep the exact boundary protected, and invoke rule resolution with the target tenant and logical time.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: minimum-age evidence
requirements.requirement: A null anchor cannot establish elapsed positive LegalMin and audit evidence records the policy actually applied.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant informed by UK GDPR Article 17(3)
requirements.requirement: Active holds prevent mutation; holds at their expiry boundary and holds at their removal boundary do not.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: hold identity scope
requirements.requirement: Holds are scoped by stable retention-entity identity, canonical record identity, and tenant, including equal canonical record and tenant identities in different retained entity types.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: strategy-consistent holds
requirements.requirement: Active holds block purge, soft delete, anonymise, and erasure execution.

requirements.source: Cohort product boundary: hosts own legal decisions
requirements.requirement: Cohort enforces configured case-specific holds but does not adjudicate their legal validity.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: race-safe hold enforcement
requirements.requirement: Mutation rechecks a concurrently created hold before purge or anonymisation.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: hold target validation
requirements.requirement: Hold creation rejects a canonical record identity when the target row does not exist.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: complete public hold race matrix
requirements.requirement: Public hold creation racing purge, soft delete, anonymise, and erasure preserves protected rows and reports committed public counts.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: hold tenant ownership
requirements.requirement: Hold creation rejects a tenant identity that does not own the existing target row.

requirements.source: Cohort contract informed by UK GDPR Article 17
requirements.requirement: Accepted erasure ignores ordinary Period and acts immediately when no positive LegalMin or active hold blocks it.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant informed by UK GDPR Article 17(3)
requirements.requirement: Positive LegalMin and active holds remain configured erasure blockers.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: exact erasure scope
requirements.requirement: Tenant, primary subject, and alternate subject matching are exact.

requirements.source: Cohort contract informed by UK GDPR Article 17
requirements.requirement: Null and future anchors are eligible without positive LegalMin and blocked and reported with positive LegalMin.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: strategy-consistent erasure
requirements.requirement: Purge, anonymise, and explicitly approved soft delete share erasure eligibility; unapproved soft delete is refused without source mutation or audit evidence.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: consistent erasure measurement
requirements.requirement: Audited dry-run erasure and live erasure report the same eligibility for purge, soft delete, and anonymise, including when LegalMin exceeds Period.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: handler-aware erasure
requirements.requirement: Audited dry-run and live handler-aware erasure apply cutoff eligibility before queueing work; dry-run invokes no handlers and persists no handler work.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: lock-wait revalidation
requirements.requirement: Handler-aware erasure rechecks the subject after waiting for a row lock and does not mutate a row whose subject changed.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: final immediate-erasure revalidation
requirements.requirement: Final mutation rechecks the post-refactor legal-minimum, hold, subject, tenant, and anchor eligibility after lock waits.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: erasure-subject metadata
requirements.requirement: Erasure-subject markers are property-targeted, permit multiple markers, are not inherited, and startup rejects incompatible effective subject types.

requirements.source: UK GDPR Article 5(1)(c), data minimisation; Cohort product invariant
requirements.requirement: Only declared anonymisation properties change; null, empty-string, fixed-literal, and factory-backed methods obey their declarations.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: atomic and scoped anonymisation
requirements.requirement: The anonymised marker is written with the mutation, original-value factories receive the original CLR value, and undeclared data remains unchanged.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: provider-aware anonymisation
requirements.requirement: Anonymisation converts provider values to CLR originals before factory invocation and converts factory output back to the provider representation.

requirements.source: UK GDPR Article 5(2), accountability; Cohort product invariant
requirements.requirement: Mutating runs persist coherent started, entity-summary, row-detail when configured, and terminal evidence whose totals agree with committed mutations.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: configurable row evidence
requirements.requirement: Per-row evidence exists when configured and resolved rule provenance is preserved in entity summaries.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: transactionally honest evidence
requirements.requirement: A rolled-back mutation does not leave committed row-detail or entity-progress evidence.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: authoritative audit ownership
requirements.requirement: Consumers cannot replace or disable the internal authoritative audit writer, and consumer observer registration cannot suppress committed authoritative evidence.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: privacy-safe diagnostics
requirements.requirement: New persisted diagnostics contain no subject data or raw exception text and carry a diagnostic identifier correlated with the original exception in structured logs; hosts remain responsible for sink access and retention.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: held-work visibility
requirements.requirement: Held work is visible in public counts and persisted entity summaries.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: skipped-work visibility
requirements.requirement: A row skipped by OnBefore is visible in public counts and persisted entity summaries.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: null-anchor visibility
requirements.requirement: Null-anchor work is visible in public counts and audited dry-run summaries.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: failed-work visibility
requirements.requirement: An entity failure is visible in the result and settles the run as partially failed without discarding successful summaries.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: tenant and subject isolation
requirements.requirement: Tenants, tenantless runs, and subject requests cannot mutate rows outside their exact scope.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: canonical record identity
requirements.requirement: Record identifiers are canonical across culture boundaries, and integer record IDs remain correctly scoped for held and tenantless rows.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: explicit schema identity
requirements.requirement: Same-named tables in another schema cannot be read, validated, or mutated.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: isolated retention DbContext scope
requirements.requirement: Caller-tracked EF entities cannot overwrite Cohort mutations.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: transactional batch accounting
requirements.requirement: An entity mutation failure does not over-report affected rows and does not undo work already committed for another entity.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: failed-handler loop prevention
requirements.requirement: Committed row-detail progress excludes a persistently failing OnBefore row from later batches in the same run rather than causing an in-run processing loop.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: cancellation evidence
requirements.requirement: Cancellation produces coherent terminal evidence and rolls back uncommitted mutation and audit progress.

requirements.source: Cohort internal invariant: cleanup exception precedence
requirements.requirement: Internal operational cleanup preserves an existing primary exception; without one, unlock failure outranks connection-close failure.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: final eligibility revalidation
requirements.requirement: A row discovered for erasure is not mutated if its subject changes while execution waits for its row lock.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: entity failure isolation
requirements.requirement: One entity failure does not suppress successful work for unrelated entities in the same run.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: tenant failure isolation
requirements.requirement: One tenant failure does not suppress later tenants or the tenantless pass in the same scheduled occurrence.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: rollback retryability
requirements.requirement: A cancelled in-flight batch leaves its source row and no committed progress evidence, so the row remains eligible for a later run.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: bounded failed-handler resources
requirements.requirement: Failed-handler progress uses no run-sized record-ID collection and candidate SQL parameter counts remain bounded by batch-local work as failures grow.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: concurrent public mutation
requirements.requirement: Concurrent public sweep engines do not double-mutate or double-report rows across relational bulk, handler-aware relational, and anonymisation implementations.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: current-schema compatibility
requirements.requirement: A public sweep succeeds against the current migrated PostgreSQL schema.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: capability-driven hosted startup validation
requirements.requirement: Real hosted startup validates every possible dynamic strategy before execution.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: direct runtime readiness
requirements.requirement: Direct public invocation without generic-host startup enforces readiness, caches only success, and fails before Started evidence.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: migration history safety
requirements.requirement: The stable-entity-identity migration backfills retained audit and hold history, the row-detail RecordId rename preserves historical evidence, and the legacy Cohort schema upgrades to the current model shape.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: scheduled kill switch
requirements.requirement: The worker reloads the kill switch between passes and stops further scheduled mutation when it becomes active.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: scheduled advisory lock
requirements.requirement: A worker skips a scheduled occurrence while another instance holds the sweep advisory lock.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: provider configuration
requirements.requirement: Hosted startup rejects a DbContext with no configured provider. Direct public execution rejects a configured non-Npgsql provider before mutation.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: hosted schema readiness
requirements.requirement: Hosted startup rejects a legacy or incomplete Cohort schema before retention execution.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: bounded hosted configuration
requirements.requirement: Options validation rejects audit observer timeouts and dispatcher numeric values above their safe ceilings, and real hosted binding rejects dispatcher values above those ceilings before execution.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: invariant-safe retention rules
requirements.requirement: RetentionRule rejects invalid period, legal-minimum, strategy, and audit states; exposes get-only properties; and has no public positional Deconstruct method.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: immutable category capabilities
requirements.requirement: RetentionCategoryCapabilities is non-empty, contains only defined strategies, defensively copies input, and cannot be mutated through its public contract.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: capability-bounded runtime resolution
requirements.requirement: Runtime rejects unresolved categories and rules whose strategy is outside startup-validated category capabilities.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: resolution context fidelity
requirements.requirement: Rule resolution preserves category, tenant, logical time, and alias path, and alias cycles report through RetentionAliasCycleException.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: explicit Cohort schema mapping
requirements.requirement: ConfigureCohortTables maps all five Cohort tables to public by default and to the exact supplied custom schema when configured.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: retained-table schema identity
requirements.requirement: A retained table with no explicit or model-default schema resolves to public, while a model-default schema is adopted exactly.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: exact PostgreSQL catalog and function resolution
requirements.requirement: PostgreSQL catalog relations and built-in functions used by Cohort cannot be shadowed by an earlier writable search_path schema.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: single schema authority
requirements.requirement: One infrastructure-local schema contract owns all five Cohort table capabilities and is consumed by model construction, adoption, and runtime validation.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: post-commit observer isolation
requirements.requirement: Multiple observers receive committed lifecycle events in order; failure, timeout, and cancellation non-cooperation by one observer cannot block later observers or alter the run result.

requirements.source: Cohort product boundary: observer delivery durability
requirements.requirement: External audit observer delivery is best effort and non-durable; authoritative database audit tables remain the durable evidence source.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: historical diagnostic preservation
requirements.requirement: Forward migrations preserve historical sweep_run.Error and sweep_row_handler_status.LastError values byte-for-byte.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: scheduled tenant orchestration
requirements.requirement: Duplicate tenants execute once in first-seen order using the first context; conflicting contexts warn; execution is sequential; null tenant entries fail before any pass; cancellation from tenant acquisition or iteration propagates without later passes; and tenant failure does not suppress later or tenantless work.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: dispatcher ceilings and time safety
requirements.requirement: Dispatcher numeric options enforce documented ceilings, timestamp and retry arithmetic saturate, poll and heartbeat waits use OperationalTime.DelayAsync chunking, and the audit observer timeout has its own validated ceiling.

requirements.source: Cohort internal invariant: bounded cleanup cancellation
requirements.requirement: Operational cleanup uses an independent bounded cancellation token while preserving primary, unlock, and close exception precedence.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: explicit consumer surface
requirements.requirement: The whole exported package API is allowlisted; authoritative audit infrastructure, engines, schema descriptors, SQL helpers, reflection helpers, and ordering helpers remain internal; a clean packed-package consumer can restore, compile, and run.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: compilable package documentation
requirements.requirement: Every C# README example is explicitly marked as a package compilation contract and compiles in a clean consumer restored from the packed Cohort package.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: complete historical migration chain
requirements.requirement: Empty and legacy databases migrate to the current schema while stable retention-entity identity and the row-detail RecordId rename preserve historical holds, summaries, and row details.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: host-owned custom-schema move
requirements.requirement: Hosts changing Cohort schema move all five tables together with a host-owned migration that preserves data, indexes, checks, foreign keys, readiness, and runtime behavior in the destination schema.

requirements.source: Cohort product invariant: immutable shipped migration sources
requirements.requirement: Every checked-in historical migration source and designer file has an approved filename and SHA-256 hash; the mutable model snapshot is excluded, and additions or edits require explicit baseline review.

requirements.source: Cohort product boundary
requirements.requirement: Cohort does not claim complete GDPR compliance, adjudicate legal requests, or determine whether host legal minima and holds are legally justified.

requirements.source: Cohort product boundary
requirements.requirement: Data-subject discovery, identity verification, consent, lawful-basis assessment, portability, rectification, and regulatory reporting remain host responsibilities.

requirements.source: Cohort product boundary
requirements.requirement: Guaranteed external audit delivery, historical error redaction, SQL Server, SQLite, and automatic source generation are outside the supported contract.
